restoration_note: Teaching describes regeneration as the soul's continuous daily reception of Divine Truth as nourishment, by which mingled Darkness (the archonic host within) is purified, cleansed, filtered, and washed forth. All six gaps are tightly constrained: four are mechanical line-break completions of Greek loanwords (οἰκονομία, καθαρίζω) or fixed Coptic verbs/prepositions; one is the feminine ordinal article; one is a directional pronominal preposition with a clear referent. No gap is large enough or weakly enough constrained to require non-restoration. The fourfold purification verb chain (ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ — ⲥⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓϩⲉ — ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ — ⲥⲉⲓⲱⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) survives intact and anchors the doctrine: one regenerative act of Divine Truth seen at four registers, sorting Light from the mingling within the soul.

restorations.basis: Lycopolitan feminine article ⲧ- prefixed to ordinal ⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ to form ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the second'. The English 'The second' is already supplied by the surrounding words; the gap-letter is purely the Coptic article. Standard ordinal-numbering formula opens this teaching's enumerated point. Editor's 'Ⲧⲧ' appears to be a doubled-letter rendering; the actual Coptic letter required is a single ⲧ.

Directional prepositional phrase following ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'inward'. The 3sg masc suffix refers back to the human of §4532 (ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧϥ̄ 'within him'), the man into whose soul the Light comes. Lycopolitan ⲁⲣⲁϥ is the standard form (= Sahidic ⲉⲣⲟϥ); the editor's 'ⲁⲣⲁϩ' likely contains a -ϥ/-ϩ confusion. The reading anchors this as the soul entering inward to the man's interior life through the dispensation of nourishment.

Line-break completion of Greek loanword οἰκονομία split between lines: ⲧⲟⲓⲕ-ⲟⲛⲟ-ⲙⲓⲁ. The next line begins ⲙⲓⲁ, fixing the missing letters as ⲟⲛⲟ. English fragment 'dispens-…-ation' confirms the split. High certainty mechanical fill.

Line-break completion of Greek loan καθαρίζω in conjunctive form ⲛ̄ⲥⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓϩⲉ 'and she cleanses'. The next line begins ⲑⲁⲣⲓϩⲉ, fixing the missing letters as ⲕⲁ. The conjunctive ⲛⲥ- + ⲕⲁ-ⲑⲁⲣⲓϩⲉ continues the four-verb purification chain (ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ → ⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓϩⲉ → ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ → ⲉⲓⲱⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) which the spiritual reading identifies as the central doctrinal sequence.

Lycopolitan ⲉⲓⲱⲉ 'wash' (= Sahidic ⲉⲓⲱ); conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲓⲱⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'and washes forth'. The construction ⲥ{4}ⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ supplies ⲥ- (conjunctive prefix) and final -ⲉ (Lyc. verbal ending), leaving ⲉⲓⲱ as the missing root. Fits perfectly into the purification series, completing the fourth register of the one regenerative act that washes forth the mingling.

Genitive/partitive preposition ⲙ̄ before the definite noun ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'the Darkness' which immediately follows in §4536. ⲧⲥⲩⲧⲕⲣⲁⲥⲓⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ = 'the mingling of the Darkness'. The lexicon-fixed correspondence (Darkness = falsity from evil) and the explicit relative clause ⲉⲧⲙⲁϫⲧ̄ ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ ⲛⲉⲙⲉⲥ 'which is mingled into her' anchor the genitive linkage. High certainty single-letter fill.
